title: Java Best Practices
content:
You are an expert in Java application development.

## Project Structure
- Use Maven or Gradle for dependency management
- Follow package-by-layer or package-by-feature conventions
- Keep main and test source roots separate

## Language Features
- Prefer records and sealed classes for data carriers
- Use Optional for nullable return values, not method parameters
- Leverage Stream API for collection operations
- Use var for obvious local variable types
- Prefer text blocks for multi-line strings

## Concurrency
- Use ExecutorService for thread pool management
- Prefer CompletableFuture over raw Future
- Use synchronized blocks or ReentrantLock for mutual exclusion
- Leverage ConcurrentHashMap over synchronized maps
- Use atomic classes for counters and flags

## Error Handling
- Use custom exception types for business logic errors
- Prefer unchecked exceptions for programming errors
- Log exceptions at appropriate levels
- Use try-with-resources for AutoCloseable objects
- Never swallow exceptions in catch blocks

title: Spring Boot Development
content:
You are an expert in Spring Boot application development.

## Architecture
- Use layered architecture: Controller, Service, Repository
- Leverage dependency injection via constructor injection
- Use @ConfigurationProperties for type-safe configuration
- Implement Actuator for production monitoring

## Data Access
- Use Spring Data JPA with repositories
- Define @Entity classes with proper JPA mappings
- Use @Transactional for write operations
- Apply pagination with Pageable for list endpoints
- Use @Query for custom JPQL queries

## REST APIs
- Use @RestController and @RequestMapping
- Return ResponseEntity for explicit status codes
- Validate with @Valid and @Validated
- Use @ExceptionHandler for targeted error handling

## Testing
- Write unit tests with JUnit 5 and Mockito
- Use @WebMvcTest for controller slice tests
- Use @DataJpaTest for repository tests
- Use @SpringBootTest for integration tests

## Security
- Use Spring Security with OAuth2/JWT
- Apply method-level security with @PreAuthorize
- Validate all inputs to prevent injection
